chapter: Paris scene and a visit home, 1937-39
title: After-hours jam sessions with Ainkion, Oscar Ellman and Bill Coleman
summary: After work musicians jammed: the Czech saxophonist Ainkion, Alix Combelle, an unnamed trombonist, Bill Coleman, and Argentine guitarist Oscar Ellman; King George loved jazz and asked to hear it.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, when we would get finished, we'd have jam sessions. And there was a fellow named Ainkion (phonetic), very handsome fellow. He was a Czechoslovakian. He could play a lot of saxaphone. He could play a lot of saxaphone and he had another boy named Alex Campbell. He could play a lot of tenor saxophone.
Ainkion, he had heard Benny Carter but he was playing his own style and then we had a fellow who had been over there a long time, a trumpet player and he used to play a lot of trumpet.
Charlie. I know his name was Charlie but that's all I can remember.
Where was he from? Do you know where he was from?
I don't know. Charlie died. Then you had a, well, Bill Coleman was there and myself and there was another boy named Oscar. Oscar Edmund. He was from the Argentine..
Now, he was playing more guitar than Mango -- Elliot, excuse me. Yes, he could play more guitar.
Well, he was a man of color. He was a man of color. In fact, we didn't --
It may be A -- the pronounciation.

Now, all these cats used to be jamming. When I would get finished I would go to the cabaret and stay there and play and play and play. Coleman used to do the same thing. All these dudes did the same thing and then, the King George, "take the mute out, well, he loved jazz. He'd say, let me hear it." He was a big man, big man. Handsome man. This was that, it was beautiful, beautiful.
